underwords.theological_sense: With the Beginning, read as the eternal uncreated Son sharing the work of creation with the Father
underwords.english_main_verse_remains: In the Beginning [of His Power] God — He shaped the Heavens and the Earth.

footnote.english: The word with is an owner-selected binitarian interpretive under-word for the Hebrew prefix בְּ (bə) in Genesis 1:1. Hebrew bə can express instrumental 'with/by' in other contexts, but the usual contextual reading of בְּרֵאשִׁית here is temporal, 'In the Beginning.' Brent A. Strawn (2022) argues for a possible 'With Wisdom/Beginning' exegetical reading; the owner's identification of the Beginning with the eternal uncreated Son who created with the Father is a further Christian canonical interpretation (John 1:1–3; 1 Corinthians 8:6; Colossians 1:15–17). This is NOT an independently established instrumental Hebrew translation of Genesis 1:1, NOT a proven lexical identification of Jesus with רֵאשִׁית, and NOT a claim that the Son was created.
